why: The real failure is the same person committing now as `Ana Souza <...@users.noreply.github.com>`, now as `ana <ana@empresa.com.br>`: the public history starts carrying the personal e-mail and `git shortlog` counts two people where there is one. The pass side has TWO commits with the identical identity, so a rule that counted commits instead of distinct name/e-mail combinations would fail there and the proof would accuse.
